1.text:
The verse begins with "All praise is for Allah Who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light", a single phrase whose parts are taken one at a time below. Its first word is praise, given to Allah alone. The verse fixes whom the praise belongs to before it turns to the people. "Who created the heavens and the earth" gives the reason for it, and the reason is the largest thing a person can see, the sky above and the ground below. The next clause, "and made darkness and light", widens the view from those two great spaces to the two states in which everything in them is seen, the night and the day, so that creation is taken as one whole. Then the turn comes, "Yet the disbelievers set up equals to their Lord in worship", and the word "Yet" is the pivot of the verse. After the praise and the proof of creation, the people who have seen all of it still set up equals. The phrase "set up equals" names the act, and "to their Lord" makes it more serious, because the equal is placed beside the very one who made the sky, the ground, the night and the day. The closing words, "in worship", show where the equal is set, which is in the act of worship and not in some other matter. The verse moves from the greatness of the Creator to the strangeness of those who ignore Him. The verses that follow take up the same Creator in other lights, as the one who made the human being from clay and who knows what is hidden in the heart. Taken together, the opening of this sūrah sets the praise first, so that every later argument about idols and signs rests on the fact that one God made everything.

**What the praise is for.**

Allah praises and glorifies His Most Honorable Self for creating the heavens and earth, as a dwelling for His servants, and for making the darkness and the light to benefit them in the night and the day. (1. All praise be to Allah, Who created the heavens and the earth, and originated the darkness and the light, yet those who disbelieve hold others as equal with their Lord.)(2. He it is Who has created you from clay, and then has decreed a stated term. And there is with Him another determined term, yet you doubt.)(3. And He is Allah, in the heavens and the earth, He knows what you conceal and what you reveal, and He knows what you earn.) He begins by lauding Himself, thereby praising Himself with His own beginningless laudation and reporting of His own self-sufficient brilliance and unitary elevation. This is praise of the tremendous Lord, the wise Enactor. Praise which means to describe in beautiful terms be ever established to God is this meant to be informative so that one believes in it? These are three possibilities the most likely of which is the last as the Shaykh Jalāl al-Dīn al-Mahallī states in his commentary on sūrat al-Kahf Q. 181; Who created the heavens and the earth — He singles out these two for mention because for the observer they constitute the most awesome visible creation; and He appointed He created darknesses and light that is every darkness zulma and every light the use of the plural only in the case of the former is because it darkness has many causes; and this is one of the proofs of His Oneness; then those who disbelieve despite the existence of this proof ascribe equals to their Lord they worship others equally.

**Why darkness and light are named in different numbers.**

In this Ayah, Allah describes darkness in the plural, Zulumat [where Zulmah is singular for darkness], while describing the light in the singular, An-Nur, because An-Nur is more honored. Similarly, by mentioning zulumat' (darkness, or layers of darkness) in the plural, and 'nur' (light) in the singular, the indication given may be that nur or light signifies the correct way and the straight path - and that is just one, while zulumat, or many layers of darkness, signifies the path of error - and their number runs in thousands. And zulumat (darkness) has been given precedence over nur (light) perhaps because zulumat is basic to this world while nur is associated with particulars - when they are there, there is light; and when they are not there, there is darkness. The hint implied is that darkness and light are not independent and self-existent like the heavens and the earth, instead, they are contingents and attributes.

**The heavens and the earth as the work of one maker.**

In this verse, samawat' (heavens) has been mentioned in the plural while 'ard (earth), in the singular - though, in another verse (65:12), earth has been identified as being seven like the heavens. Also noticeable here is that the origination of the heavens and the earth has been expressed through the word, 'khalaqa' (created) while that of darkness and light with the word, ja‘ala' (made). The system inherent in the governance of heaven and earth is so perfect in its coordination and its unitary nature—despite the magnitude of the task—that it proclaims aloud the fact that its Creator and Organiser can be none other than the one and only God. The flawlessly regulated revolution of the earth in space around the bright sphere of the Sun and, hence the coming into existence of light and darkness and day and night are events beyond human comprehension. It has also been said that heaven is an allusion to the heaven of recognition, which is the hearts of the recognizers. And on his authority from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding Allah's saying (Praise be to Allah) he said: '(Praise be to Allah) Allah says: gratitude and godhood are Allah's, (Who hath created the heavens) in two days: By saying in this verse of the Holy Qur'an that Allah Ta ala is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and He is the Maker of darkness and light, all such false notions have been refuted - when He is the sole Creator and Maker of everything, ascribing partners to His Divinity makes no sense. He decorated heaven with the form of the stars, adorned it with sun and moon, and made it the gaz ing place of the earth-dwellers. In the same way, He adorned the heaven of recognition with the sun of knowledge, the moon of tawḤīd, and the stars of thoughts, and then He made it the gazing place of the heaven-dwellers.

**Who the disbelievers take as partners.**

(Yet those who disbelieve hold others as equal with their Lord.) meaning, in spite of all this, some of Allah's servants disbelieve in Him and hold others as partners and rivals with Him. Some of Allah's servants claimed a wife and a son for Allah, hallowed be He far above what they attribute to Him. Despite all this, some of His servants disbelieve Him and associate partners with Him. (Yet those who disbelieve) the unbelievers of Makkah (ascribe rivals) idols (unto their Lord). As for the disbelievers and polytheists of Arabia, they demonstrated such philanthropy in dishing out Godhood that, according to them, every piece of rock on a hill could be good enough to become an object of worship for the whole human-kind! Similarly, the Christians who, despite professing the creed of Tauhid, started taking Sayyidna Isa and his blessed mother as partners in the divinity of God - and then, in order to prop their belief in one God, they to rely on the irrational theory of Unity in Trinity. Some of Allah's servants claimed a wife and a son for Allah, hallowed be He far above what they attribute to Him. The polytheists in India take an incredibly high number of gods as partners in the divinity of God. The Arya Samajists, despite acknowledging Tauhid, take spirit and matter to be infinitely pre-existent, and independent of the power and creation of God, whereby they have moved way away from the reality of Tauhid.

**The night and the day as proof.**

He created the night and the day, which follow one another. The fact is that the wonderful system by which everything in the world is regulated is in itself proof that its Lord is one and one alone, and this same system also demonstrates that God is so great that He does not need any assistant either in His creation or in His control of what He has created. By pointing out to the reality of Tauhid (Oneness of Allah) and its open proof in this verse the purpose is to warn all those peoples who do not simply believe in Tauhid, or have forsaken the reality of Tauhid despite professing it. By saying in this verse of the Holy Qur'an that Allah Ta ala is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and He is the Maker of darkness and light, all such false notions have been refuted - when He is the sole Creator and Maker of everything, ascribing partners to His Divinity makes no sense.

2.text:
The second verse turns from the people's worship to their own beginning, and it keeps the same voice as the first. "He is the One Who created you from clay" points back to the Creator named in the previous verse, and it brings the reader down to the material of the human body. The clay is the start of the account, and the verse does not stop there. "then appointed a term" moves the account forward to the end of each life, which is the term of death, and the phrase "for your death" marks that meaning as the one the verse intends. "and another known only to Him" gives a second term that no one can see, and "for your resurrection" names it, so the life between the first clay and the last return is bounded at both ends by a fixed time. The whole phrase "then appointed a term for your death and another known only to Him for your resurrection" carries the two terms together. The verse ends with "yet you continue to doubt", and the word "yet" joins it to the verse before, where the people set up equals after the proof had been given. The doubt is the same failure in a new place, since the people who were made from clay and who will be raised again still refuse to believe in a second life. The verse does not hide what it asks of them, which is to see that the one who began them is the one who ends them and the one who raises them.

**What the clay is and who was made from it.**

(He it is Who has created you from clay,) refers to the father of mankind, Adam, from whom mankind originated, multiplied in numbers and spread about, east and west. It is He Who created you from clay by creating your father Adam from it; then He decreed a term for each of you at the conclusion of which you die. He, may He be glorified, is the One Who created you, O people, from clay when He created your father, Adam ﷺ from it. (He it is Who hath created you from clay) i.e. from Adam and Adam was created from clay, (and hath decreed a term for you) He created this world and fixed a term for its extinction and made created beings whose lifespan expires with death. His clay pertained to the World of the Creation, and his spirituality to the World of the Command. The verse is saying that Allah is the One who created Sayyidna Adam with clay, and then, gave him life - and common human food comes from the moist substance of clay, and from food the sperm, and from the sperm comes the creation of the human being.

**The term known and the term hidden.**

(Then has decreed a stated term. And there is with Him another determined term...) His saying;. (Then has decreed a stated term,) refers to death, while,. (And there is with Him another determined term...) refers to the Hereafter, according to Sa'id bin Jubayr who reported this from Ibn 'Abbas. (And then has decreed a stated term,) is the term of this earthly life, while,. A term is stated fixed with Him for your resurrection; yet thereafter you O disbelievers doubt you are uncertain about the Resurrection when you know that it was He Who initiated your creation and One Who has the power to initiate creation is even more capable of bringing you back to life after death. He also fixed another term, which only He knows, when He will raise you back to life on the Day of Rising. (It is He, Who takes your souls by night (when you are asleep), and has knowledge of all that you have done by day, then He raises (wakes) you up again that a term appointed (life) be fulfilled.)[6:60] The meaning of Allah's statement,. (And there is with Him another determined term) refers to man's extent of life until he dies as mentioned in Allah's statement;. (And then has decreed a stated term,) is the term of this earthly life, while,. In such circumstances, man is unable to understand how the eternal world of the Hereafter, which will be free from grief ( 35:34) can come into existence. (With Him) is that none but Him knows when it will occur. (The knowledge thereof is with my Lord. None can reveal its time but He.)[7:187], and,. (They ask you about the Hour – when will be its appointed time? You have no knowledge to say anything about it. To your Lord belongs (the knowledge of) the term thereof.)[79:42-44] Allah said,.

**Why the term is fixed with Him.**

(A term is fixed with Him) Allah knows the term of the Hereafter: therein there is no death or evanescence. Then He, may He be glorified, fixed a period for your stay in the life of the world. If one were to make a start from this point, right from the beginning to the end - birth, living, death among a great mesh of internal dimensions and distances - it would show that the belief in the Oneness of Allah is a reality all too clear. It is about this that the verse said: ; (He is the One who created you from clay, then destined a term). After that, comes the mention of the end of the whole world, that is, the Qiyamah, in the following words: , that is, there is yet another term which stands fixed and which is known to Allah alone. (And there is with Him another determined term...) refers to the Hereafter, according to Sa'id bin Jubayr who reported this from Ibn 'Abbas.

**Why you still doubt the raising.**

Despite this, you still doubt about His ability to raise you back to life. (Yet still you) O people of Makkah (doubt) in Allah and resurrection after death! The words: ‌ (And the fixed term lies with Him, yet you are in doubt) carry the instruction that using the personal death of a human being as the proof of the general and collective death of the whole world system, that is, the Qiyamah, is something very natural and logical. Summing up in a sequence, we can say that, in the first verse, we have been told about the big universe', that is, the whole wide world, which has been created and made by Allah Ta ala.

**The clay, the spirit, and what came from the earth.**

What pertains to creation is "He fermented Adam's clay in His hand. " What pertains to the command is I have blown into him of My spirit [15:29]. In Adam were both rose garden and field of clay, so the clay was the place of roses. The body of a human being is wholly made of earth elements but it has unique properties, none of which is found in the earth. If a living and active man comes into existence from earth; if fragrant flowers and luscious fruits emerge from earth, then why cannot a more perfect world emerge from our present world?

3.text:
The third verse states who God is, and it does so in the place where people live and where the sky is seen. "He is the Only True God in the heavens and the earth" repeats the claim of the first verse with the word "Only", so no part of the sky or the ground is left to another god. The verse then moves inward from the heavens and the earth to the hidden life of the people under them. "He knows whatever you conceal and whatever you reveal" covers what is kept in the heart and what is spoken in the open, and the two halves balance so that nothing falls between them. The final clause, "and knows whatever you do", brings the knowledge from thought and speech to action, so the whole person is in view. The verse carries the consequence of the two verses before it. Having shown the maker of creation and the one who fixed the terms of life, it now shows that the same One sees what people hide and what they do in the open. The verses after it turn to the signs that the people keep turning away from.

**What the Only True God means in the heavens and the earth.**

He is God the One worthy of being worshipped in the heavens and in the earth. He, may He be glorified, is the One worthy of worship in the heavens and the earth. (It is He Who is God in the heavens and the earth.)[43:84] meaning, He is the God of those in heaven and those on earth, and He knows all affairs, public and secret. (He is Allah in the heavens) He is the God of the dwellers of heaven (and in the earth) and the God of all the dwellers of the earth. It declares that Allah is the only Being who is worthy of worship and obedience in all the heavens and the earth, and He is the One who knows everything human beings conceal or reveal and, particularly, everything they say or do. Meaning, it is He Who is called Allah, throughout the heavens and the earth, that is, it is He who is worshipped, singled out, whose divinity is believed in by the inhabitants of the heavens and the earth.

**What He knows of your secrets and your speech.**

He knows your secrets and your utterance what you keep secret and what you utter openly among yourselves and He knows what you earn what you do of good and evil. He knows what you keep hidden in your breasts just as He knows what you make public, (and He knoweth what you earn) of good or evil. He knows the intentions, statements and actions you keep hidden and those you make public; and He will judge you about them. If the world of the Hereafter is to be created with some matter other than that of this world, that is something beyond man’s ken; but if the other world of the Hereafter is to be created from the matter of this world, it has to be conceded that this world in itself lacks the capacity to bring into existence a world of total perfection.

**Being in the heavens and in the earth, and where He is.**

One can say that He is in heaven through Essence, everywhere through knowledge, in the spirit through companionship, and in the soul through proximity. He does not take up place through need, but rather displays places through mercy. He who sees You is concealed in vision, and he who seeks You is neither on earth nor in heaven. The soul comes to nothing in Him, and He takes the place of the spirit that comes to nothing in Him. Allah praises and glorifies His Most Honorable Self for creating the heavens and earth, as a dwelling for His servants, and for making the darkness and the light to benefit them in the night and the day. The third verse contains the consequential outcome of what was said in the first two verses. If a living and active man comes into existence from earth; if fragrant flowers and luscious fruits emerge from earth, then why cannot a more perfect world emerge from our present world? 4.text:
The fourth verse describes how people act when a sign reaches them. "Whenever a sign comes to them from their Lord" sets the sign in a plain order: it comes from the Lord, it comes to them, and it comes again and again, so the word "Whenever" shows that the signs are not rare. "they turn away from it" gives the response, and it is a turning away, the body moving off, which is the picture the verse paints. The verse does not name the sign in this place, but the signs in view are the proofs of the Oneness of God, given in the Qur'an and in the world around the people. The phrase "from their Lord" keeps the source of the sign in view, and "they turn away" marks the distance people choose to put between themselves and what they are shown. The verse is a complaint about heedlessness, and it links back to the verse before, where the Lord was shown to know what the people hide. The next verse turns to what happens to people who turn away in this way once their rejection has been made plain.

**What a sign is in this verse.**

Clear evidences and proof of the Oneness of Allah, as well as miracles proving the truthfulness of the messengers, have now come to them; yet despite this, they turned away and paid no attention to these signs and miracles. ‌ ‌ 4 that is, despite the many clear proofs and open signs of the Oneness of Allah, the dissenters and rejectionists among human beings have taken to a way of their own, using which, they would turn their faces away from whatever sign is shown to them for their guidance, without ever paying the least attention to it. And never an Ayah comes to them from the Ayat of their Lord, but that they have been turning away from it Indeed, they rejected the truth when it came to them, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock at Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you? (Never came there unto them) i.e. unto the people of Makkah (a revelation of the revelations of Allah) such as the eclipse of the sun or the splitting of the moon or stars (but they did turn away from) except that they disbelieved in i.e. the sign. (Indeed, they rejected the truth when it came to them, but there will come to them the news of that which they used to mock at.)

**Why the proof is turned away from.**

Allah states that the rebellious, stubborn polytheists will turn away from every Ayah, meaning, sign, miracle and proof that is evidence of Allah's Uniqueness and the truth of His honorable Messengers. The reason for this is that all these proofs, in spite of all their clarity, always appear through a veil of cause and effect. When these signs come to a man’s attention, he attributes them to certain causes and pays no heed to them. No proof or miracle from their Lord comes to the idolaters except that they ignore it without paying any attention. Allah advises and warns the disbelievers, that they should avoid the torments and afflictions of this life, similar to what befell their likes from previous nations, who were stronger, wealthier, had more offspring, and were more exploitive on the earth.

**Heedlessness, the cause of the complaint.**

The fourth verse carries a complaint against the anti-truth doggedness and obstinacy of the chronically heedless human race by saying: He does not become inclined to accept their validity. This Ayah contains a warning and a stern threat for the disbelievers' rejection of the truth, stating that the disbelievers will surely know the truth of what they used to deny and taste the evil end of their behavior. The reason for this is that all these proofs, in spite of all their clarity, always appear through a veil of cause and effect. When these signs come to a man’s attention, he attributes them to certain causes and pays no heed to them.

**The rain and the destruction of earlier peoples.**

And We poured out on them rain from the sky in abundance, and made the rivers flow under them. Yet We destroyed them for their sins, and created after them other generations. (And created after them other generations.) so that We test the new generations, as well. Yet, they committed similar errors and were destroyed, as their ancestors were destroyed. Therefore, beware of the same end that might befall you, for you are not dearer to Allah than these previous nations, but the Messenger whom you defied is dearer to Allah than the Messengers they defied. Allah advises and warns the disbelievers, that they should avoid the torments and afflictions of this life, similar to what befell their likes from previous nations, who were stronger, wealthier, had more offspring, and were more exploitive on the earth. (Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you?) meaning, they had more wealth, children, buildings, abundant provision, riches and soldiers.

5.text:
The fifth verse states the result of the turning away in the verse before it. "They have indeed rejected the truth when it came to them" uses the word "indeed" to confirm that the rejection is real, and "when it came to them" makes clear that it was not a rejection of something far off, but of the truth as it arrived at their door. "so they will soon face the consequences of their ridicule" moves from the act to its outcome, and the word "soon" matters, since the consequence is not put off to a remote day. "the consequences" is the thing they will meet, and "their ridicule" names what caused it, which is the mocking they aimed at the message. The verse answers the heedlessness described before it, and the verb "rejected" is the main act of the sentence, stood in the past so that the act is already done, because it shows that the mocking will come back to those who did it. The verses after it recall the peoples who were destroyed before the people of Makkah, and the link is the same: the sins of those peoples brought them to a fate they had not expected.

**Rejecting the truth when it came.**

This Ayah contains a warning and a stern threat for the disbelievers' rejection of the truth, stating that the disbelievers will surely know the truth of what they used to deny and taste the evil end of their behavior. While they have turned away from these clear evidences and proofs, they had previously turned away from something even clearer: they denied the Qur’ān that Muhammad ﷺ brought. (And they) the people of Makkah (denied the Truth) the Qur'an and the sign (when it came unto them) when Muhammad ﷺ came to them. Allah states that the rebellious, stubborn polytheists will turn away from every Ayah, meaning, sign, miracle and proof that is evidence of Allah's Uniqueness and the truth of His honorable Messengers.

**What the punishment is and when it comes.**

They denied the truth the Qur’ān when it came to them but there shall come to them the news the consequences of what they were mocking. (But there will) this is a threat of punishment (come unto them the tidings of that which they used to deride) the news of their derision and the punishment of their derision on the Day of Badr and the Day of Uhud as well as on the Day of the Confederates. They will soon realise, when they see the punishment on the Day of Rising, that what they used to mock and what he brought to them was in fact the truth. (Now, there shall come to them the full account of what they have been laughing at). Allah advises and warns the disbelievers, that they should avoid the torments and afflictions of this life, similar to what befell their likes from previous nations, who were stronger, wealthier, had more offspring, and were more exploitive on the earth. This overweening confidence on their part increases to such an extent that they even become unafraid of God. There will be a Reckoning (Hisab) when everyone will have to account for one's faith and deed - and everyone shall get the reward or punishment for what he or she has done. But, believing and confessing at that time is not going to work for them because that will be no day of deeds - rather, that day will be the day of Retribution. He challenged every eloquent and learned master of words in Arabia to match the Word brought by him. Allah Almighty has given the respite - a God-sent piece of luck, so to say.

**Why they make fun of the message.**

Those who have firmly established themselves in this world, having accumulated many material goods for themselves, and who see the manifestations of their own greatness and popularity around them, are always liable to be a prey to misunderstanding. They look down upon the things God has gathered around the caller of Truth as compared to the things around them. They make fun of the warning given by the missionary of Truth that, if their arrogance continued, their material achievements would not be able to save them from God’s scourge. It means that right now these people who are heedless to their fate mock at the miracles and commandments of Allah brought by the Holy Prophet and at the all true message that there is a Qiyamah (Doomsday) and Akhirah (Hereafter), but very soon will come the time when all these realities will be before their eyes. But his' antagonists, who would have not hesitated to sacrifice anything they had - life, wealth, honour, children, family, anything, anytime - just to defeat him, did not have the courage to accept his challenge and, at the least, produce one 'Ayah (verse) like the 'Ayah of the Holy Qur'an. Their treatment of the dayee as a non-entity makes his warnings also insignificant.

**Other peoples who were overtaken.**

Even historic instances of God’s having destroyed materially well set up people, as if their lives were of no value whatsoever, fail to teach them a lesson. The recurrence of events in which one set of people face decline while another set rises shows that the rule of ‘crime and punishment’ is prevalent here, but man does not learn a lesson from this. (Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you?) meaning, they had more wealth, children, buildings, abundant provision, riches and soldiers. The succeeding generations repeat those very same actions as were indulged in by their predecessors, due to which they were destroyed.

6.text:
The sixth verse asks a question and then answers it with a list of events. "Have they not seen how many disbelieving peoples We destroyed before them?" opens with a question that expects the answer yes, so the reader is asked to look back at the past before the verse states anything. The word "seen" matters, because it asks people to observe what they can see for themselves, in their travels and in the ruins of earlier nations. "We had made them more established in the land than you" gives the comparison, and it is a hard one, since those peoples had more power and more standing than the people now addressed. "We sent down abundant rain for them and made rivers flow at their feet" describes the blessings they were given, so that the reader sees how much had been given before the punishment. "Then We destroyed them for their sins and replaced them with other peoples" gives the turn, the sins and then the replacement, and the verse ends with the fact that nations are swapped one for another. The verse links to the verse before it, which named the consequence of mockery, and it shows the same consequence in the history of the earlier peoples. Each step of the list is a word the reader can point to in the verse itself. The reader is given the same question twice, once as a question and once as a list, so that the list answers it. The whole list is built so that the one who hears it can name each step, from the question to the blessing to the sin to the replacement.

**What the question asks them to see.**

Have they not seen in their travels to Syria and to other places how many kam is predicative and not interrogative meaning ‘many’ a generation how many a community of past communities We destroyed before them; We established them We assigned them an established place in the earth through strength and abundance as We have not established as We have not assigned you there is a shift in the address here from third person to second; and how We unleashed the heaven the rain upon them in torrents one torrent after another and made the rivers to flow beneath them? beneath their dwellings. Do these disbelievers not know Allah’s custom of destroying communities who do wrong? (Have they not seen how many a generation before them We have destroyed whom We had established on the earth such as We have not established you?) meaning, they had more wealth, children, buildings, abundant provision, riches and soldiers. Those who have firmly established themselves in this world, having accumulated many material goods for themselves, and who see the manifestations of their own greatness and popularity around them, are always liable to be a prey to misunderstanding. In the first verse, it was said about the people of Makkah, the direct addressees of the Holy Prophet : ‌ ‌ Havethey not seen how many generations We have destroyed prior to them?' Here, seen' means to ponder about, because these generations were not present before them at that time to see. In the present verses, the same deniers of the truth have been given an opportunity to learn and correct themselves by observing conditions around them as well as those prevailing in times before them.

**The rain and the rivers given before the destruction.**

Allah sent down successive rains upon them and made rivers flow beneath their homes; yet they then went against Him, so He destroyed them because of the sins they committed. (and We poured out on them rain from the sky in abundance,) in reference to rain that comes often,. (And made the rivers flow under them.) as rain was abundant and the springs were plentiful, so that We deceived them. (See they not) were the people of Makkah not informed in the Qur'an (how many a generation) past nations (We destroyed before them, whom We had established) We gave them sovereignty and respite (in the earth more firmly than We have established you) than the sovereignty and respite We have given you, O people of Makkah, (and We shed on them abundant showers from the sky) whenever they needed it, (and made the rivers flow beneath them) beneath their fields, plantations and trees.

**Why they were destroyed for their sins.**

Then We destroyed them because of their sins because of their denial of the prophets; and We raised up after them another generation. (Yet We destroyed them for their sins) meaning the mistakes and errors that they committed,. (Yet We destroyed them for their sins) We destroyed them because of denying the prophets, (and created after them another generation) a different people who were better than they. About past peoples of the world, first it was said that the kind of power and well-being given to them was not given to people later than them, but when these very people took to the ways of belying prophets and disobeying Divine injunctions, all that majesty of power and wealth was rendered futile against the punishment of Allah which annihilated them totally. Even historic instances of God’s having destroyed materially well set up people, as if their lives were of no value whatsoever, fail to teach them a lesson. The succeeding generations repeat those very same actions as were indulged in by their predecessors, due to which they were destroyed.

**Other generations created after them.**

(and created after them other generations,) for, these generations of old perished and became as legends and stories,. (And created after them other generations.) so that We test the new generations, as well. Yet, they committed similar errors and were destroyed, as their ancestors were destroyed. At the end of the verse, it was said: ‌ ‌ (and raised up, after them, another generation). At the end of the verse, it was said: ‌ ‌ (and raised up, after them, another generation).

**The lesson for the people now addressed.**

So, this was a lesson for the addressees of today, the people of Makkah who did not have the power of the legendary people of Ad and Thamud, nor the affluence of the people of Syria and Yaman. For them, the need of the hour was to learn a lesson from what happened to the peoples of the past and turn towards an examination of their doings and think where they are going to end up by op-posing the truth. Therefore, beware of the same end that might befall you, for you are not dearer to Allah than these previous nations, but the Messenger whom you defied is dearer to Allah than the Messengers they defied. Thus, you are more liable than them to receive torment, if it was not for Allah's mercy and kindness. It means that the great power of Allah Jalla Sha'nuhu was not simply limited to seeing that nations of strength, authority and power lay destroyed in a flash, but it was right there on the ashes of their destruction that other peoples were made to rise and populate places, as if nothing had happened there and no one was missing from the scene. This spectacle of Divine power and wisdom is something observable in its own ways during every time and period when thousands die every day but there is no vacuum left anywhere. We never come to realize that people who belonged here are not here anymore. Once, while on the plains of Arafat with a million men and women spread around, came the thought that only a mere seventy or eighty years earlier, none among this whole assembly of people existed. Yet, on this same place of Arafat, nearly that many other human beings were present, no trace of whom exists today. No doubt, events of the past are documents full of chastening lessons which, if seen to find wisdom, would prove to be more effective than a thousand sermons. Perhaps, it is for this reason that the Holy Qur'an has taken the essence of history as a server of warning and a dispenser of good counsel.

7.text:
The seventh verse describes a demand that the disbelievers would have made even if it had been granted, and it turns on the word "Had". The whole opening clause, "Had We sent down to you O Prophet a revelation in writing and they were to touch it with their own hands", sets the supposition, and the Prophet is named in the middle of it, between the sending down and the writing, so the reader hears that the revelation is addressed to him and is not only described. The verse begins with "Had We sent down to you" as a supposition, so the reader knows that the thing described did not happen and the reply is about what would have been. "a revelation in writing" names the form, a book on paper that can be held in the hand. "and they were to touch it with their own hands" describes the test they would have used, the sense of touch they would have trusted, and it shows how far they were asking for proof that could be handled. "the disbelievers would still have said" is the sharp part of the verse, because it means that even the proof they asked for would not have changed their minds. The last words, "This is nothing but pure magic!", give the answer they would have offered. The verse links to the verses before it, where the same people refused the signs, and it shows that the refusal is a settled habit and not a matter of missing evidence. The Prophet is addressed directly, so the verse also gives him the comfort of knowing what was never going to change.

**Why a book written on paper would not have been enough.**

(And even if We had sent down unto you a Message written on paper so that they could touch it with their hands,) meaning, if they saw this Message's descent and were eye-witnesses to that,. For example, if Allah were to send down, as they demanded, a written book from the heavens - and not only that they see it for them-selves that there is no sleight of hand or sight or magic, they may even physically touch it with their hands to make sure that they were not day-dreaming and that it was a reality - still, after all that, they would say nothing but: Similarly, if a book complete in every detail, comes down from the sky, he will say, ‘This is mere magic,’ to justify his rejection of it. If we had sent down to you, O Messenger, a book written on paper and they had seen it with their eyes, they would not have accepted it out of stubbornness and denial; and they would have said, ‘What you have brought is nothing more than clear magic; and we will never believe in it’. The second verse was revealed in the background of a particular event when Abdullah ibn Umaiyyah came up with a hostile demand before the Holy Prophet by saying: I cannot believe in you until such time that I see you climbing all the way to the heavens and bringing a book from there before our eyes, in which it should be written in my name that I should attest to your prophethood.' And, on top of saying all this, he went on to even declare that he would still not be impressed enough by his accomplishing all that for he does not seem to be likely to convert to Islam anyway. (And even if We opened to them a gate from the heaven and they were to continue ascending thereto. They would surely say: "Our eyes have been (as if) dazzled. Nay, we are a people bewitched.")[15:14-15], and,. It is a mercy from Allah to His creation that He sends every type of creation, Messengers from among their kind, so that they are able to call their people to Allah, and their people able to talk to them, ask them and benefit from them. And had We revealed to you a Scripture inscribed on parchment as they requested and had they then touched it with their hands — this is more powerful than saying ‘had they seen it with their eyes’ since it touch is more effective in eliminating doubt; the disbelievers would have said in disobedience and obduracy ‘This is nothing but manifest sorcery’.

**The demands they made and what they reveal.**

Such were the uncalled-for and hostile demands made and mocking and insulting dialogues inflicted on the Holy Prophet especially when he himself was more affectionate for his people, more than their own parents could ever be to them. They were a kind of people who would not stop at what they were demanding. This is because what they are saying comes from malice and hostility. The reason for a man going astray in this world is that here he has complete freedom to reject the Truth. What effect these caustic bad manners would have made on his heart is something we cannot fathom. If the preacher of God’s word appears in the shape of an ordinary man, the ‘reason’ given for ignoring him could be that his effectiveness hinges on a talent for leadership and has nothing to do with Truth or righteousness. If the hidden realities were revealed and God and His angels made their appearance, there would be no question of prophethood or of giving the call of Truth, because thereafter nobody would dare to deny the realities.

**The disbelievers and the magic they would name.**

(the disbelievers would have said: "This is nothing but obvious magic!") This is similar to Allah's description of the disbelievers' defiance of facts and truth,. Even if they were presented with far more clear proofs of their Prophet's veracity, they would still not believe. The people of Makkah used to ask, if the Prophet was appointed to convey God’s message, why God’s angels were not with him to testify. (And even if We opened to them a gate from the heaven and they were to continue ascending thereto. They would surely say: "Our eyes have been (as if) dazzled. Nay, we are a people bewitched.")[15:14-15], and,. Similarly, if a book complete in every detail, comes down from the sky, he will say, ‘This is mere magic,’ to justify his rejection of it. Consequently, even if the angels descend, while the disbelievers still had the same attitude, then the torment will surely befall them from Allah as a consequence.

**Comfort for the Messenger.**

Therefore, to comfort him, it was said that such demands from his antagonists were not being put forward for any useful purpose, nor did they want to follow it. It can only be sensed by one who is consumed with the good of his people in the same manner as the blessed Prophet himself was. They assess him on the basis of his outward appearance and, finding him insignificant in that respect, they deny him. O Muhammad, by Allah we will not believe until you bring us a book from Allah along with four angels with it, bearing witness that it is from Allah and that you are His messenger , and so this verse was revealed . God’s Messenger appears to them like an ordinary man suddenly emerging and claiming very high status. (And indeed Messengers were mocked before you, but their scoffers were surrounded by the very thing that they used to mock at.) comforts the Messenger concerning the denial of him by his people. The Ayah also promises the Messenger , and his believers, of Allah's victory and the good end in this life and the Hereafter. The Ayah also promises the Messenger , and his believers, of Allah's victory and the good end in this life and the Hereafter.

8.text:
The eighth verse returns to the demand for an angel and sets out what would follow if it were met. "They say, Why has no visible angel come with him?" gives the demand in their own words, and the word "visible" is the key to what they want, since they are asking for an angel they can see with their own eyes. The phrase "with him" points at the Prophet, so the request is for proof that comes beside him. "Had We sent down an angel" is the start of the reply, and it is a supposition, so the reader is asked to see the result before anything happens. "the matter would have certainly been settled at once" gives that result in full. The matter would be settled, which means the case against them would be decided, and "at once" marks that the decision would come straight away, with no interval left in between. "and they would have never been given more time to repent" closes the thought, because the time to repent is the period they still have, and a visible angel would take it from them. The verse turns the demand around so that the people see the cost of what they asked for, which is the loss of the chance to turn back. The demand and the reply are set side by side on purpose, so that the request and its result can be read together. The verse links to the one before it, where the Lord was shown to know what the people hide, and it prepares the verse after it, where the angel is sent in another form. The sight they wanted is set against what they could bear, and the whole passage is built to show that a sign they could see would end their chance to believe.

**Why the matter would be decided at once.**

(If We sent down an angel) as they are asking you, (then the matter would be judged) he would come down to punish them and take away their souls; it is also said that this means: if the angel comes down, he would destroy all of them; (no further time would be allowed them (for reflection) they would not be allowed any delay. In other words, it means If We do send the miracle they demand, that is, send an angel, then, these people who are not the kind who would accept truth will still act contrary and hostile even after having seen the miracle, then, the Divine command to have them destroyed would stand activated. "Why has not an angel been sent down to him" Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been judged at once, and no respite would be granted to them And had We appointed him an angel, We indeed would have made him a man, and We would have certainly caused them confusion in a matter which they have already covered with confusion And indeed Messengers were mocked before you, but their scoffers were surrounded by the very thing that they used to mock at Say: (And had We appointed him an angel, We indeed would have made him a man, and We would have certainly caused them confusion in a matter which they have already covered with confusion.) meaning, if We send an angel along with the human Messenger, or if We send an angel as a Messenger to mankind, he would be in the shape of a man so that they would be able to speak to him and benefit from his teachings.

**Why there would be no respite.**

Since they would be given no respite after that hap-pens, therefore, they should understand that the fact of not showing the miracle demanded by them spells out real good for them, without which they would be nowhere. If we send down an angel of the kind they wish, we will destroy them if they do not believe; and they will not be given time to repent. These disbelievers said, ‘We will believe if Allah sends down an angel with Muhammad ﷺ who speaks to us and bears witness that he is a messenger’. Consequently, even if the angels descend, while the disbelievers still had the same attitude, then the torment will surely befall them from Allah as a consequence. (We send not the angels down except with the truth (i.e. for torment, etc.), and in that case, they (the disbelievers) would have no respite!)[15:8], and,.

**What an angel would mean if it were sent.**

(On the Day they will see the angels, no glad tidings will there be for the criminals that day.)[25:22] Allah's statement,. (Why hath not an angel been sent down unto him?) to testify for what he is saying. One answer Allah gave to them was that by making such demands, these heedless people were inviting their own destruction, because the Divine law is that, should a people ask their prophet to show a miracle of their choice, and as a result of their demand, such miracle is shown by the power and will of Allah, then, should they, even then, remain reluctant to believe and accept faith any longer, they are destroyed by a mass general punishment. It is a mercy from Allah to His creation that He sends every type of creation, Messengers from among their kind, so that they are able to call their people to Allah, and their people able to talk to them, ask them and benefit from them. In this case, the angel (in the shape of a human) will also cause confusion for them, just as the confusion they caused themselves over accepting humans as Messengers!

**The demand that they made.**

This time their demand was: We shall believe in you only when you go and bring a book from the heavens and let four angels come along with it to testify that the book was from none but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah.'. (They say) i.e. 'Abdullah Ibn Umayyah al-Makhzumi: And they say ‘Why has an angel not been sent down to him?’ to Muhammad to confirm his truthfulness; yet had We sent down an angel as they have requested and if they then did not believe the matter that they be destroyed would have been decreed and then they would not be given any respite they would not be given any extra time for repentance or an excuse as is God’s custom in dealing with those before them destroying them when they disbelieve after their request is granted. The third verse was also revealed because of an event which concerns this very Abdullah ibn Abi Umaiyyah who, accompanied by Nadr ibn al-Harith and Nawfal ibn Khalid came to the Holy Prophet . (And indeed Messengers were mocked before you, but their scoffers were surrounded by the very thing that they used to mock at.) comforts the Messenger concerning the denial of him by his people. These particular people of Makkah were really not making their demands as based on any good intentions, which may have at the least given some hope of their accepting the truth.

9.text:
The ninth verse states what would happen if an angel were sent in a form the people could bear. "And if We had sent an angel" begins with a supposition, the same as the verse before, and "We would have certainly made it assume the form of a man" describes the one way an angel could be seen by people on earth, which is in human shape. The verse then gives the result, "leaving them more confused than they already are". The word "confused" names the state they would be in, and the phrase "than they already are" shows that they are already in confusion, so a visible angel would add to it and not clear it. The verse answers the demand in the verse before. It shows that the angel could not be seen without taking the form of a man, and that the sight of a man would bring the same doubt the people already have. The reader is asked to notice the word "already", which places the confusion before any sign is given. It links back to the verse about the visible angel, and it prepares the next verse, which turns to the messengers who came before and were mocked. Every part of this verse is a step in the same argument, from the angel to the man to the doubt that stays in place.

**What the angel in the form of a man would bring.**

This is because they will not be able to look at the angel due to light." (Had We appointed an angel) as Our messenger, (We assuredly had made him a man) in the form of a man such that they are able to look at him; (and (thus) obscured for them) the real form of the angel they obscure) the traits and description of Muhammad. Firstly, an angel may come as he is, in his form and state of being. The second form in which the angel could come down is that the angel comes in human shape and form, as Sayyidna Jibra'il al-Amin has come to the Holy Prophet several times in the shape of a human being.

**Why the angel would be seen as a man.**

If I had sent an angel to them, I would have made him in the form of a man, so that they could listen and learn from him, as they would not be able to learn from an angel in the original form that I created him. If so, no human being can stand before his real awe - in fact, he is more likely to die at the never imagined sight. (And they say: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?") to convey the Message with admonition along with him. One answer Allah gave to them was that by making such demands, these heedless people were inviting their own destruction, because the Divine law is that, should a people ask their prophet to show a miracle of their choice, and as a result of their demand, such miracle is shown by the power and will of Allah, then, should they, even then, remain reluctant to believe and accept faith any longer, they are destroyed by a mass general punishment. These particular people of Makkah were really not making their demands as based on any good intentions, which may have at the least given some hope of their accepting the truth.

**The angel as a messenger sent down.**

And had We appointed him the one who is sent down to them an angel We would assuredly have made him the angel a man that is We would have sent him in the form of a man so that they would be able to see him since no human being is capable of seeing an angel; and had We sent him down and made him a man We would have assuredly confused obscured for them what they are confusing for themselves when they say ‘This is but a mere mortal like the rest of you’. And even if We had sent down unto you a Message written on paper so that they could touch it with their hands, the disbelievers would have said: Therefore, it was said: ‌ ‌ (And had We sent down an angel, the whole matter would have been finished). In this situation too, the Holy Prophet is told, this questioner will have the same objection against this angel' as he has against you - because he would take him to be nothing but human.

10.text:
The tenth verse turns from the angel to the messengers who came before the Prophet, and it gives comfort by telling of their fate. The verse begins with "Other messengers had already been ridiculed before you O Prophet", and the word "already" means that mockery of the messengers is an old pattern and not something new that should be taken as a sign against him. "before you" joins the Prophet to the line of messengers who went before, so he is not alone in what he suffers. "but those who mocked them were overtaken by what they used to ridicule" gives the outcome, which is the same as the consequence named in the fifth verse: the mockers were caught by the thing they laughed at. The word "overtaken" describes the arrival of the punishment, and the phrase "what they used to ridicule" makes the link explicit, since the thing they joked about became the thing that struck them. The verse closes the passage on the angel by setting the mockers of every age under one rule. It links to the verse before and to the fifth verse, and it leads into the verses that call the people to look at the earth and the past.

**Messengers before the Prophet were mocked too.**

(And indeed Messengers were mocked before you, but their scoffers were surrounded by the very thing that they used to mock at.) comforts the Messenger concerning the denial of him by his people. Other prophets and messengers before him had to face similar heart-breaking experiences, but they did not lose hope. (Messengers (of Allah) have been derided before thee) their people derided them as your people are deriding you now, (but that whereat they scoffed surrounded) befell (such of them) of the unbelievers (as did deride) the punishment of their derision. And messengers were indeed mocked before you — this is meant as a consolation for the Prophet s — but those who scoffed at them were encompassed by that which they mocked namely by the punishment sent down on them those who mock you will be encompassed likewise. If these people poke fun at you by asking for an angel to be sent down with you, then communities in the past also poked fun at their messengers.

**The mockers were overtaken by the punishment.**

Then the punishment, which they used to deny and mock when they were warned about it, surrounded them. Allah sent torment, afflictions and punishment on them in this life, as well as the painful torment in the Hereafter, while saving His Messengers and believing servants. After having answered all these hostile questions, solace has been given to the Holy Prophet in the fifth verse by saying that this attitude of mockery and injury directed against him by his people is not something particular to him.

**Why doubt veils the truth from the mockers.**

This is because they will not be able to look at the angel due to light." (And they say: "Why has not an angel been sent down to him?") to convey the Message with admonition along with him. The real test of man is that he should be able to tear down the veil of doubt and raise himself to the position of certainty. Is there a combination of opposites in God’s regime, given that He seems to have filled man’s world with oppression and injustice and the rest of the world with mercy and meaningfulness? This is because God has ordained that the Truth be veiled in doubt, so that man may find reasons for rejecting it alongside arguments in support of its acceptance. Since they would be given no respite after that hap-pens, therefore, they should understand that the fact of not showing the miracle demanded by them spells out real good for them, without which they would be nowhere. In this world communicating the Word of God is a task of some complexity. He should eschew doubt in all its guises and take a firm hold of the divine Truth.
